status.en: 220 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Kaduna.
status.nb: 220 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen have escalated attacks across northern Nigeria, killing Islamic scholar Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka in his home and killing multiple civilians in Plateau, including seven in one community and a 60‑year-old woman harvesting groundnuts. In eastern Nigeria, gunmen killed at least ten people, while in Taraba state a mass shooting in Binnari left 62 dead and dozens injured. Kidnappers abducted six residents in Kaduna and three vigilantes died in a separate Plateau incident. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn har eskalert angrepene i Nord-Nigeria, drept den islamske lærde Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka i hans hjem og drept flere sivile i Plateau, inkludert syv i ett samfunn og en 60‑år gammel kvinne som høstet jordnøtter. I Øst-Nigeria drepte væpnede menn minst ti personer, mens en masseskyting i Binnari i Taraba-staten etterlot 62 døde og dusinvis sårede. Kidnapperne bortførte seks innbyggere i Kaduna, og tre voktere døde i en separat hendelse i Plateau. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
